secrets.description: GitHub App ID for the bot account that owns app repos. Without this, app creation fails and no PRs can be opened. `default: ""` lets a self-app staging clone boot for UI work — github.init() degrades to disabled when this is empty (see services/github.js).

PEM private key for the GitHub App. Single-line with literal \n escape sequences; the loader un-escapes at startup. `staging_default: ""` pairs with GITHUB_APP_ID — both empty means github.init() takes the disabled branch and staging boots without GitHub features.

Classic PAT with `repo` scope for the bot user. Powers repo creation, branch pushes, PR creation, and the in-app feedback flow (Issues:write on USERNODE_PLATFORM_REPO). `staging_default: ""` lets staging boot — every consumer guards on `if (!pat)` and degrades.

Platform-wide fallback Claude key. Users can override with their own via BYOK; if neither is set, Mayor-driven flows are unavailable. Already optional, so no staging fallback needed — staging just inherits the unset state.

Anthropic ADMIN API key (`sk-ant-admin…`) — NOT the same credential as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY above, and not interchangeable with it. Used read-only for GET /v1/organizations/cost_report, which backs the "Anthropic credits" row in the hamburger status area (#555). Optional: with it unset, that row falls back to an estimate derived from the platform's own spend ledgers and says so. No staging_default — staging inherits the unset state, which is exactly the fallback path a reviewer should see.

Bootstrap admin username. The first row in `users` is created with this name and is_admin=true on first boot. `default: "admin"` covers self-app staging (this key is deploy-owned, so the panel renders it read-only and no value is ever stored for it); the staging DB clone already carries whatever admin row prod has, so this default only matters for a fresh-DB clone.

Bootstrap admin password. Hashed at first boot — rotating only takes effect on a fresh DB or via direct SQL update. `private` keeps a self-app-staging container from receiving the prod admin password (would let any PR reviewer log in as admin to prod). `staging_default` is a config.js boot-sentinel only — never used to authenticate. Self-app staging containers expose no usable password login: the cloned `users.password` column is replaced with `__staging_redacted__` by db-manager.scrubPrivateColumns, and staging admins authenticate via the parent-issued iframe JWT instead (see SELF-HOSTING.md "Self-staging — iframe-auth login flow" and middleware/auth.js).

Cookie-signing secret for express-session. Required at boot. Rotating invalidates every active session cookie. `private` for parallel reasons to JWT_SECRET — staging must never sign cookies that browsers honor for prod. `staging_default` is a deliberately distinguishable dummy so any cookie minted by staging is obviously not a prod cookie.

Postgres superuser password the platform connects with. Used by docker-compose.yml to seed the postgres container, by db-manager.js to spawn per-app databases, and baked into DATABASE_URL for the platform itself. Rotating means rolling the postgres container too. `private` blocks staging propagation of the prod DB superuser. `staging_default` is a placeholder — the staging container's DATABASE_URL is set explicitly to the staging clone's URL by services/staging.js, and db-manager.js falls back to 'localdev' when this is unfamiliar; spawning child apps from within a staging container is out of scope for UI-edit workflows.

Platform's on-chain wallet public key for the Usernode social-vibecoding linking flow (chain-poller + auth wallet-link in routes/auth.js). When unset, wallet-linking is gracefully disabled — the platform still works without it.

Private counterpart to USERNODE_APP_PUBKEY. Pre-staged in deploy.yml so any future platform-originated wallet-send flow can use it without a redeploy — currently no runtime consumer reads it. Always set together with USERNODE_APP_PUBKEY. `private` blocks staging propagation: this key signs real on-chain transactions with real funds.

platform_env.description: Log verbosity for the platform process: DEBUG, INFO, WARN or ERROR. Raising it to DEBUG is the one tunable you actually want to change without a code change while chasing something in prod.
Ceiling on concurrent worker containers across the whole platform. The committed default targets ~50 concurrent users on a 20-core/62GB box; raise it only alongside WORKER_MEMORY headroom.
Ceiling on concurrent worker containers per user. Stops one person from consuming the whole global budget.
Docker memory limit for each worker container, in docker's own units (e.g. `1280m`). MAX_GLOBAL_SESSIONS × WORKER_MEMORY is the worst-case worker footprint.
Docker CPU limit for each worker container.
Maximum Postgres connections in the platform's pool. Must stay comfortably under the postgres container's own max_connections.
How long a worker container may sit idle before it is evicted to free a session slot.
Idle time before an active chat session is auto-paused. Paused sessions keep their state but release their worker.
How often the session sweeper runs the autopause/eviction pass.
When `true`, resuming a session under global pressure evicts the least-recently-used worker instead of refusing the resume.
Minimum age a session must reach before pressure-driven LRU eviction may take its worker.
How long an idle staging container survives before it is torn down. Staging is rebuilt on demand, so this trades disk and memory against the wait on the next preview.
Age at which an open proposal is flagged stale and its author notified.
Grace period after the stale notification before the proposal is archived.
How long archived proposals are retained before deletion.
How often the stale-proposal sweeper runs.

How often the fast governance-apply ticker applies vote-passed rename / env-var / close-issue / campaign proposals whose merge window has elapsed. Set to 0 to disable it (the hourly stale-proposal sweeper still applies them).
How long to wait for Caddy to obtain a certificate for a newly-published app subdomain before giving up on the warm-up.
Threshold above which a certificate probe is logged as slow.
Seconds docker waits after SIGTERM before killing a container. Raising it makes deploys slower but gives in-flight requests longer to drain.

The at-rest key: services/secrets.js derives AES-256-GCM from it, and every stored BYOK Anthropic key, app secret and platform-variable value is encrypted under it. Deploy-owned (from the USERNODE_JWT_SECRET repo secret) and NOT settable here — the values in this very table are encrypted with it. NEVER rotate: decrypt() returns null silently, orphaning every ciphertext. Boot exits 1 without it.

RSA-2048 PKCS#8 private half (RS256) of the app-identity pair that signs the per-user token the shell injects into app iframes. Asymmetric on purpose: containers get only the public half, so an app can verify a user but never forge one. Deploy-owned, single-line PEM with literal \n escapes. Boot exits 1 without it, and round-trips a probe token so a mismatched pair fails loudly at startup.

SPKI public half of the app-identity pair, same single-line-PEM convention. The only platform key ever handed to a child container — it can verify, never sign — so it is deliberately not marked private. Deploy-owned; must be generated TOGETHER with the private half or the boot pair-check fails. Boot exits 1 without it. Dormant until the phase-2 iframe cutover; validated at startup regardless.

HMAC key for the tokens worker containers present to the internal API (middleware/internal-auth.js, anthropic-proxy-auth.js). Its own authority: never placed in any container — workers receive only the minted capability token. Deploy-owned (openssl rand -hex 32). Safe to rotate: warm workers holding a stale token get evicted and re-bootstrap. Boot exits 1 without it; under 32 bytes only warns.

HMAC key for private-app edge grants and the scoped __usernode_access per-host cookie (routes/internal.js, services/app-access.js). Both purposes share this key and are separated by an explicit pur claim, so a 120s grant cannot be replayed as a 12h cookie. Deploy-owned; use a DIFFERENT openssl rand -hex 32 from the worker secret. Safe to rotate — people just re-authorize. Boot exits 1 without it.

Shared secret checked against the X-Ingest-Key header on the two ingest writes, POST /api/v4/slot-outcomes and /api/v4/epoch-stats (middleware/topochain-auth.js). `openssl rand -hex 32`. Unset never blocks boot — ingest writes just 500 until set. Sole caller is usernode's observability-hub-receiver, which needs the same value at its v4 cutover. Rotates independently of the partner key.

Shared secret compared against the partner group's X-API-Key header (src/middleware/topochain-auth.js#partnerApiKey). Generate with `openssl rand -hex 32` and hand it to partner API callers at their /api/v4 cutover. Unset doesn't block boot — every partner-group request returns 500 'API key authentication not configured.' until it is set. Rotates independently of TOPOCHAIN_INGEST_API_KEY.

Base URL of the external zkPassport bridge service that verifies proofs for POST /api/v4/mobile/zkpassport/complete (src/services/topochain/zk-bridge.js). Unset doesn't block boot — every zkpassport/complete call returns 500 'The zkPassport bridge is not configured.' until it is set. Not secret, so it stays visible in the console for is-it-pointed-at-the-right-host checks.
Allows authenticated mobile users to register encrypted FCM destinations and starts the durable activity-notification sender. Requires PUSH_ENV plus matching Firebase credentials.
Trusted environment partition embedded in every push payload and checked by Flutter, for example production or staging. It must match the mobile build exactly.

Authoritative Firebase project ID returned to mobile registration clients and expected in the service-account document. Required while mobile push is enabled; sending fails closed when the credential differs.
Complete Firebase Admin service-account JSON encoded as base64 on one line. Required only while MOBILE_PUSH_ENABLED is true; never forwarded to child apps.

Which transport sends platform mail: auto (default), gmail, http, or log. auto tries Gmail, then the generic HTTP API, and in production sends nothing rather than printing login codes into the log. Naming a provider explicitly means a missing key is reported as broken, not silently downgraded. A staging preview ALWAYS logs instead of delivering, whatever this says.

The From address on every platform mail. Defaults to Usernode <no-reply@usernodelabs.org>, which is the single sender for all platform mail, so a fresh deploy needs no edit here. The mailbox behind GMAIL_OAUTH_* must be authorised to send as this address (a Workspace alias or a 'send mail as' identity) or every send is rejected upstream. Not secret — it is in the header of every mail we send.

OAuth2 client ID of the Google Cloud 'Desktop app' credential used to send platform mail through the Gmail API. All three GMAIL_OAUTH_* keys must be set together — a partial config sends nothing. Unset never blocks boot: the mail flows still report success while delivering nothing, which is why Admin → Topochain → Settings shows an explicit mail card.
OAuth2 client secret paired with GMAIL_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID. Private: encrypted at rest and never returned by any API.

Long-lived refresh token minted once for the sending mailbox with the https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send scope. Private: it can send mail as your domain indefinitely, so it is encrypted at rest and never returned by any API. Note the platform-variable value constraints (src/services/platform-env.js): no single quote, no CR, no NUL, 8192 characters max.

Global ceiling on outbound mail per rolling hour, across all recipients and kinds. Bounds the provider bill and the sender-reputation damage from a runaway loop or an abusive burst; per-recipient caps (5 login codes/hour, 1 waitlist confirmation/day) are fixed in code. Sends over the ceiling are recorded as suppressed_rate_limit and visible in the admin mail card.

HTTPS send endpoint for the generic HTTP mail provider — used when PLATFORM_MAIL_PROVIDER is http, or when auto finds no Gmail config (Resend: https://api.resend.com/emails). POSTed as JSON with a bearer token; body shape lives in src/services/mail/transports/http-api.js. All three TOPOCHAIN_MAIL_* keys must be set together — a partial config sends nothing.

Bearer credential for TOPOCHAIN_MAIL_API_URL. Private: it can send mail as your domain, so it is encrypted at rest and never returned by any API. Only used by the http transport — one of several providers.
Legacy sender address, kept as a fallback for deploys configured before PLATFORM_MAIL_FROM existed. Prefer PLATFORM_MAIL_FROM; this is only consulted when that is unset. Not secret.

Comma-separated hosts whose https redirect URIs a chat product may register against the /mcp connector (subdomains match too). This is what keeps dynamic client registration from being an open redirect registry: only widen it to a host you would hand a consent screen to. An explicit value REPLACES the default rather than extending it. Loopback is accepted only in local-development mode.

Client ID of the GitHub OAuth app that links a Usernode account to a GitHub one (scope `public_repo`), so the connector can fork an app into the user's own account for their coding agent to push to. Falls back to WAITLIST_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID. Unset: the link routes 404, Settings says so, and prepare_work answers github_link_unavailable and names the platform-build fallback.

Client secret paired with GITHUB_LINK_CLIENT_ID. Private: it can mint GitHub authorizations for this deployment, so it is encrypted at rest and never returned by any API. Falls back to WAITLIST_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET. Both halves must be set together — an id without a secret counts as unconfigured and degrades exactly as described on GITHUB_LINK_CLIENT_ID.

Apex domain the platform and every app subdomain live under. Set from a GitHub repo variable by the deploy and listed here for documentation only — changing it needs the DNS and certificate change to land in the same breath, so it is deliberately not editable in the console.
Commit the running container was built from. Written by the deploy workflow from `github.sha`; documentation only.
Platform Postgres connection string, assembled by docker-compose from USERNODE_DB_PASSWORD. Documentation only — it is a reserved key and can never be written from here.
